subs.finding: You report a strong foundation in personal aims and recognising inherited expectations. Test it through a more demanding decision and independent feedback.
subs.action: Test a new opportunity against your aims and review the trade-off with an independent mentor.
subs.progress: Explain why the role supports your aims, or propose a credible alternative.

subs.finding: You report a strong foundation in understanding family values and choosing what to carry forward. Test it through a more demanding decision and independent feedback.
subs.action: Lead a discussion of a difficult value conflict and record the reasons for the agreed choice.
subs.progress: A reasoned decision connects values to consequences and acknowledges another view.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in reflecting on wealth and identity and discussing privilege and responsibility. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Write what family wealth enables, what responsibilities it creates and which choices you want to make independently. Discuss one tension with a trusted mentor.
subs.progress: You can describe your own position without relying on the family's preferred account.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in choosing a possible family role and keeping alternatives open. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Draft a role proposal covering contribution, time, authority and support. Include an alternative outside the family, then discuss a time-limited trial with a sponsor.
subs.progress: Desired roles and limits are explicit; a trial or next conversation is agreed.

subs.finding: You report a strong foundation in knowing how wealth was created and understanding turning points. Test it through a more demanding decision and independent feedback.
subs.action: Test an inherited lesson against a present challenge and explain where circumstances have changed.
subs.progress: A short timeline separates established facts, different recollections and questions still open.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in understanding how the business earns money and recognising strategic risks. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Ask an operating leader to explain customers, margins, cash needs and competitive pressures. Prepare a one-page account of the business model and two material risks.
subs.progress: An operating leader confirms your account and corrects any misunderstandings.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in knowing key people and their roles and locating knowledge and authority. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Map key executives, advisers and stakeholders. For each, record their role, decision authority and knowledge held; identify one dependency on a single person.
subs.progress: Relevant officeholders confirm the map and one continuity dependency is addressed.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in understanding branches and generations and anticipating effects on relationships. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Discuss a possible ownership or leadership change with representatives of relevant branches. Record their stated interests separately from your assumptions.
subs.progress: A shared issue map identifies common aims, competing interests and matters requiring discussion.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in knowing assets and holdings and distinguishing legal and operational roles. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Prepare an authorised entity map. For each relevant interest, separate ownership, benefit, management and fiduciary roles; ask counsel to confirm how they differ.
subs.progress: You can explain the main roles, information rights and matters requiring specialist confirmation.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in reading financial information and understanding risk and liquidity. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Review an actual financial pack with the finance lead. Explain profit, cash and distributable funds, then identify a liquidity or concentration risk and prepare three questions.
subs.progress: You can explain the figures and one risk in your own words, with corrections recorded.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in understanding the purpose of entities and understanding rights and restrictions. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Review relevant structures with qualified counsel. Record each purpose, your actual or possible rights, restrictions and who can exercise authority; mark anything unconfirmed.
subs.progress: Counsel confirms the summary and you can explain what the structure permits and limits.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in forming capital principles and questioning recommendations. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Write principles for spending, investing, giving and preserving capital. Apply them to one proposal and question its downside, liquidity, fees and effect on other people.
subs.progress: Your decision note states reasons, unanswered questions and the expertise needed.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in understanding decision processes and identifying who has authority. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Select three decisions: a dividend, a senior appointment and an asset sale. Identify who proposes, approves, implements and is consulted; confirm with relevant officeholders.
subs.progress: A confirmed decision-rights map records consent requirements and unresolved boundaries.

subs.finding: You report a strong foundation in expressing disagreement respectfully and asking questions without fear. Test it through a more demanding decision and independent feedback.
subs.action: Lead a substantive challenge while acknowledging evidence that could change your own view.
subs.progress: You can raise uncertainty and disagreement constructively within the agreed process.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in separating relationships from duties and handling competing interests. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Take part in a bounded decision involving different interests. State your role, identify conflicts, compare options and record how the decision and dissent were handled.
subs.progress: The record explains the trade-off, decision process and any conflict or unresolved concern.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in understanding governance bodies and experiencing formal meetings. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Observe two authorised meetings. Record how the agenda, evidence, challenge, decision and follow-up work, then debrief with the chair or sponsor.
subs.progress: You can explain how a decision was reached and identify one improvement to follow-up.

subs.finding: You report a strong foundation in building experience outside the family and receiving independent assessment. Test it through a more demanding decision and independent feedback.
subs.action: Apply one practice learnt outside the family to a bounded family project and compare results.
subs.progress: An external assessor identifies demonstrated strengths and an improvement to make.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in making decisions with consequences and learning from setbacks. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Lead a limited project with agreed budget, decision limits and a review date. Keep a decision log and examine one setback with a sponsor.
subs.progress: Delivery and feedback show what worked, what failed and what you would change.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in developing relevant skills and obtaining objective feedback. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Agree two skills required for a possible role. Set a practical exercise, an independent assessor and a review date for each, then apply the feedback.
subs.progress: You can demonstrate each skill in practice and explain how feedback changed your approach.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in recognising limits of personal expertise and selecting and questioning advisers. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Prepare an adviser meeting around the objective, options, assumptions, fees and incentives. Afterwards, explain the recommendation, one alternative and when another specialist is needed.
subs.progress: You can assess the advice and explain selection criteria; appointment powers are confirmed separately.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in knowing the current generation's expectations and having your own aims understood. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: You and the current generation separately record desired roles, timing and limits. Compare the accounts with a sponsor and record agreements and differences.
subs.progress: Mutual expectations are explicit; open differences have an owner and a further discussion date.

subs.finding: You report useful foundations in having a gradual transfer process and having opportunities to practise. A practical exercise can establish where further preparation is needed.
subs.action: Agree one staged responsibility with a sponsor. Specify information access, decision limits, support, success criteria and a review before any wider delegation.
subs.progress: A role brief and completed supervised exercise show whether the next stage is justified.

subs.finding: Your answers suggest limited preparation in knowing duties after incapacity and knowing immediate contacts and responsibilities. Clarify the gap before accepting responsibility in this area.
subs.action: Walk through an unexpected absence. Confirm contacts, document locations, access and your actual powers for the first 48 hours; record every dependency on one person.
subs.progress: A response sheet is rehearsed, authority is confirmed and gaps have named owners.

subs.finding: You report a strong foundation in forming intentions for future influence and acting with an independent identity. Test it through a more demanding decision and independent feedback.
subs.action: Sponsor a bounded improvement and test whether its results support your original intention.
subs.progress: A reasoned stewardship proposal acknowledges consequences and leaves room for your own approach.
